text:
sophia: Quick kickoff: product wants a tight battlecard + two landing copy variants for the launch blog and webinar. Focus: competitive surface vs cloud-managed endpoints, bare LLM APIs, and DIY infra. Ship by tomorrow morning?

alex: On it. We should lead with outcomes for engineering teams (predictable tail latency, unit economics, and operational guardrails).

nora: Suggested hooks for webinar: 1) 'Predictable latency at production scale', 2) 'From prototype to SLA: rollout + rollback', 3) 'Avoiding costly outages with smart routing'. Short demos: rollout canary, KV cache speedup, and model-fallback.

sophia: Love it. Keep legal-safe language: no competitor logos or explicit product names (use CloudA / API-B / DIY). legal-bot: noted.

ben: Quick bench snippet (internal dev run, 95th pct, 4k tokens): Redwood Dedicated: 110ms; CloudA managed endpoint: 230ms; API-B: 340ms; DIY multi-tenant: 420ms. Footnote: sample workload; not representative of all models.

eli: For battlecard one-liners: Cloud-managed: "Fast to pilot; unpredictable unit economics at scale"; LLM APIs: "Great for prototyping; lack ops controls"; DIY infra: "Control at cost of engineering time". Add objection handlers for each.

alex: Draft objection handlers: Cloud-managed -> "We offer predictable unit economics and fallbacks to keep customer-facing features live during incidents."; LLM APIs -> "We give rollout controls, caching, and monitoring needed for production without replatforming."; DIY -> "Private gives control with lower ops tax via a managed control plane."

nora: Landing copy variants: Variant A (engineer): "Stop guessing inference costs. One API, predictable latency, and rollout controls so you ship with SLAs, not hope." Variant B (pm): "Ship reliable AI features. Unified runtime and automatic fallbacks protect users when models stumble."

sophia: Email subject lines for A/B test: "Benchmarked: lower tail latency for production LLMs", "Predictable inference economics for shipped features", "How teams avoid model outage surprises". Keep one for ops audience.

ben: Demo checklist for webinar: small chat model, open-medium model, RAG with doc store; canary 10%->50%->100%; trigger simulated slow responses to show fallback; show token-cost estimate.

eli: Inbound routing: tag "launch-inference" -> immediate email with one-pager and bench highlights; 48h follow-up with demo clip; SDR touch if sample usage > threshold or industry flagged regulated. Add Dedicated trial CTA.

sophia: Timeline: alex battlecard draft by EOD; ben benchmark artifact and visual by tonight; nora demo script + subject lines by morning. Review at 10am tomorrow.

legal-bot: Quick reminder: avoid absolute cost claims, no competitor logos, include methodology blurb on slides.

sophia: Final note: headline shouldn't be 'we're cheaper' 1 frame as 'predictable unit economics and lower ops risk'. Save assets to /marketing/webinar/prelaunch/. Ping when drafts live. :rocket:
